section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the opening header of the maamar, including the date and Torah portion.
This section explains the Gemara's statement that the purpose of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, citing Rashi's interpretation that this refers to the essence of Torah.
section.t: "A saying that is regularly in the mouth of Rava: The purpose of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, as it is said,
'The beginning of wisdom is fear of the L-rd; good understanding to all who do them,'
It does not say 'to those who study them,' but rather 'to those who do them.'
And my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, brings this in his maamar beginning "Zeh she'amar" of Shabbos Parshas Vayishlach 5689
(printed in the Kuntres of Wedding Discourses 5689)
is that it should be accompanied by repentance and good deeds.
that the essence of Torah is understanding and comprehension,
that one should understand and comprehend what one studies
for when one does not understand what one studies, it is not considered study at all],
and in this statement of our Sages, it says that the essence of Torah is repentance and good deeds.
that the reason the maamar brings Rashi's commentary on "the purpose of wisdom,"
because the meaning of "purpose" in most places is the ultimate intention,
the meaning of "the purpose of wisdom is repentance and good deeds" is,
that the ultimate intention in the study of Torah
is that it should lead to repentance and good deeds.
Therefore the maamar brings Rashi's commentary that "the purpose of wisdom" is "the essence of Torah."
For in addition to the fact that the intention of Torah study is that it should lead to repentance and good deeds,
also the very essence of Torah itself
and repentance and good deeds are seemingly two different matters.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section elaborates that wisdom and repentance are not only different but opposites, as Torah study emphasizes the student's existence while repentance and good deeds emphasize self-nullification.
section.t: in addition to being different matters,
For in the study of Torah, the existence of the person engaged in Torah is emphasized,
for the mitzvah of Torah study is that one should understand and comprehend
To the extent that even regarding a legal ruling, one must rule specifically according to one's own understanding.
"They differ in the Heavenly Academy... the Holy One, blessed be He, says... and the entire Heavenly Academy says...,"
the reason for this, that the Heavenly Academy ruled the law differently than the Holy One, blessed be He,
because according to the rules of Torah, they must rule the law according to their understanding.
This matter applies even in the study of Torah in the Heavenly Academy.
And all the more so in the study of Torah of man below,
for "the Torah is not in heaven,"
and "the Holy One, blessed be He, laughs and says, 'My children have defeated Me, My children have defeated Me.'"
And in repentance and good deeds, the self-nullification of man is emphasized.
For the matter of repentance is that a person leaves and is nullified from his own existence,
and so it is regarding mitzvos
for in addition to the fact that the fulfillment of mitzvos must be
in the manner of the service of a servant,
the action that is accomplished through the fulfillment of mitzvos is that the limbs of the person fulfilling the mitzvah become a chariot for the Supernal Will,
and a chariot is a matter of self-nullification.
